key_insight: LLMs wrote functional medical image classifiers without seeing images, but training the same architecture on just 256 labelled images performed better.
clinical_relevance: Weight-space programming may offer a research route for label-scarce medical imaging, but these results do not establish clinical readiness or replace labelled training data.
method: Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra directly generated small LeNet-style CNN weights without images, tools or training-data optimisation.
Evaluated seven classification tasks across chest X-ray, breast ultrasound, abdominal CT and pelvic MRI.
Compared against zero-shot MedSigLIP and the same CNN architecture trained with Adam.
evidence_signal: Across six MedMNIST tasks, mean test AUC was 0.719 for Opus and 0.711 for Astra versus 0.828 with 256 labelled training images; on SynthUterus, AUCs were 0.764 and 0.136, respectively.
watch_item: Astra’s below-chance pelvic MRI result, attributed to a systematic error, highlights the need for task-specific validation before any clinical consideration.
paper_title: Weight-Space Programming for Medical Imaging: Do We Still Need Training Data?
